newsitem.title: YEMEN: Execution of Yemeni killer expected on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Execution of Yemeni killer expected on Saturday.

text.p: Yemen is expected to execute in public on Saturday a man who shot dead four schoolchildren and two teachers, a judicial official said on Thursday.

"The execution of the criminal is expected to take place on Saturday," he told Reuters. "It will take place in a public place but there is a dispute among judicial officials on whether a Kalashnikov rifle will be used or a sword for beheading."
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh must ratify the death sentence against the man, Mohammad Ahmad Misleh, and the official said he expected the approval in the next 48 hours.

Yemen's supreme court on Thursday approved the death sentence ruling of a Yemeni appeals court, but overturned the part which said Misleh's body should also be nailed on a cross for three days near the site where he carried out the killings.
"The Supreme Court approved execution by firing squad but decided that the crucifixion should not take place," another official told Reuters.
Misleh opened fire with an assault rifle on hundreds of children lined up in the yards of the adjacent schools before morning classes on Sunday.
He killed a headmistress, a teacher and four children. Eleven children were injured, four seriously.
Misleh, 48, has become the focus of intense Yemeni anger since the slayings.
Thousands of people gathered near the schools on Thursday, some of them on rooftops, in anticipation of the execution.
"We are waiting for the execution," one told Reuters.
The official said judicial officials were also undecided on whether to carry out the death sentence at the site of the slayings or in another public place.
"They are still undecided on the place for the execution, whether to have it in front of the two schools or somewhere else to avoid scaring the pupils and other children.
Misleh's claim that the shooting spree was an attempt to avenge the alleged rape of his daughter and the kidnappings of his daughter and son was rejected by the appeals court.
